headline: Haena State Park and Coastal Entry Requirements
reservation: Reservations for parking, shuttle, and entry at Haena State Park are mandatory for non-residents and must be made weeks in advance. A separate permit is required for hiking the Kalalau Trail beyond Hanakapiai Valley. Official booking windows and rules for state parks are subject to frequent updates.

days.title: Canyons and Cool Highlands

stops.name: Waimea Canyon State Park
stops.detail: Stop at the main lookout to see the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific' before clouds move in.

stops.name: Kokee State Park
stops.detail: Explore the higher elevation forest and the Kalalau Lookout for views of the Na Pali cliffs from above.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours round-trip from south shore; winding mountain roads
days.note: Temperature drops at high elevations; visibility at lookouts is highly variable.

days.title: North Shore Cliffs and Bays

stops.name: Haena State Park
stops.detail: Visit Ke’e Beach for a coastal walk, ensuring you have your required advance reservation.

stops.name: Hanalei Bay
stops.detail: Walk the historic pier and enjoy the mountain backdrop of this iconic crescent-shaped bay.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours round-trip; traffic common through Kapaa and Hanalei
days.note: The road ends at Haena; verify bridge status after heavy rain as closures can occur.

days.title: Southern Coast and Heritage

stops.name: Spouting Horn Park
stops.detail: View the natural blowhole from the paved observation area near Poipu.

stops.name: Maha’ulepu Heritage Trail
stops.detail: A rugged coastal walk along limestone cliffs; stay on established paths to protect cultural sites.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes total driving; local transfers between Poipu area sites
days.note: The Maha’ulepu area is privately owned with restricted gate hours; check local access times.

intel.title: Haena Parking Logistics
intel.text: Non-resident parking at Haena is extremely limited and requires a pre-paid reservation. Using the North Shore Shuttle is recommended to avoid the parking bottleneck.

intel.title: Canyon Connectivity
intel.text: Expect no cellular signal in Waimea Canyon and Kokee State Parks. Download digital trail maps and coordinate meeting points before leaving the town of Waimea.

intel.title: West Side Services
intel.text: There are no fuel stations past the town of Waimea on the way to the canyon. Ensure your tank is at least half full before starting the steep climb to Kokee.

intel.title: Morning Lookout Priority
intel.text: Clouds often obscure the Na Pali lookouts in Kokee by midday. Arrive at the Kalalau and Pu’u O Kila lookouts early for the best chance of clear views.

intel.title: Ocean Safety Awareness
intel.text: North Shore swells in winter make many beaches dangerous for swimming. Always check the official Hawaii Beach Safety website for current conditions and lifeguard warnings.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Lihue (LIH); stop in Lihue or Kapaa for supplies before heading to your North or South shore base.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for paved roads; check rental terms for restrictions on unpaved access roads like Polihale.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset at Hanalei Pier is a classic viewpoint, though winter swells may alter the shoreline experience.
